newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reith says not moved to copy U.S. minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: Reith says not moved to copy U.S. minimum wage.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith on Friday played down speculation the government would introduce a single minimum wage similar to that in the United States.
Reith's comments backed earlier statements by prime minister John Howard that there was no need to reassess Australia's relatively high minimum wage in an effort to combat high unemployment.
Asked if the government would introduce a U.S.-style minimum wage system, Reith told reporters: "Australia is not America."
"We have some interesting parallels that you can make between Australia and the U.S., Australia and New Zealand, and Australia and Botswana.
"But in the end our industrial relations system is a unique Australian device," Reith said.
Howard said on Tuesday there was no need to change Australia's minimum wage levels to combat high unemployment, but added the community had to understand the impact minimum wage levels had on jobs.
"He (Howard) has made his comments on the public record, which have been grossly exaggerated by some," Reith said.
"He did make some comparisons between Australia and the United States which have sparked off the hyperventilation by some, but not by me," he said.
The U.S. system of a low minimum wage has been credited with helping bring down unemployment rates.
Australia's unemployment rate had been stuck above 8.5 percent since Howard's conservative Liberal-National coalition was elected in march 1996.
Unemployment rose to 8.8 percent in May but fell back marginaly to 8.5 percent for June.
The United States jobless rate rose to five percent in June after dropping to a near 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May.
